defect_observations.observation: The end-gauge measurement equation uses l, d, alpha, theta, l_S, alpha_S, theta_S without glossing them; the held source defines them (H.1.1, PDF physical 91), including that theta and theta_S are deviations from 20 C. The budget's input roles are recoverable only through the table labels, and 'Mean bed temperature' labels an input whose stated expectation is -0.1 C (the source's bed temperature is 19.9 C). Not judged coverage-defeating because the table names each input's role, but the specification would be clearer with the symbol definitions.

The end-gauge 'Evaluation' column gives arithmetic only (0.075 um/3, 10 nm/2.57, 20 nm/3, 2e-6/sqrt3, 'supplied', ...). It does not name the information source behind each row: the certificate at k=3, the comparator certificate at 95 percent from six replicates with t95(5)=2.57, the three-sigma statement, rectangular bounds, the reported bed-temperature uncertainty (H.1.3.1-H.1.3.6). It also does not say which rows are Type A and which Type B. The general definition and the conversion list explain the sources, so C03 still holds; the worked budget does not show the separation where it could.

The step Var(L) = Df(m) Sigma Df(m)^T, which joins the exact affine theorem (295-309) to the remainder bound (380-402), is never written for general f; it appears only as an instance in the impedance proof (annex 335-336). The practical formula is centered at the estimate x with assessed U ('the chosen center', 311), while the bound is centered at the mean m with model covariance Sigma. The handbook does not state that x = m and U = Sigma, or approximately so, is an additional condition; the held source 5.1.3 Note 1 makes this distinction.
The power example never names the output P as a power and gives no units for any quantity. It is not used for the C01 verdict, which rests on the end-gauge specification.

The summary of the 2026 amendment's new Note 1 to 4.1.4 omits that the note first offers a Monte Carlo method per JCGM 101:2008 as the alternative to higher-order Taylor terms (amendment printed p. 1, PDF physical 5). Procedure step 5 (744-746) refers only generically to 'a separately validated propagation procedure'.

The voltmeter case does not give the information source of the 15 uV half-width: the manufacturer's accuracy specification, 14e-6 of reading plus 2e-6 of range (4.3.7 Example 2). It also leaves the model V = Vbar + DeltaV unwritten.
